# @xano-sdk/mcp-oauth

> Hosted OAuth sign-in for Xano SDK MCP servers: a branded sign-in and consent page, the
> endpoints behind it, and the `oauth` block to pass to `mcpServer()`.
> Registers one API group (`MCP OAuth`) and four endpoints (`GET mcp_oauth/login`,
> `GET mcp_oauth/request`, `POST mcp_oauth/sign_in`, `POST mcp_oauth/complete`) onto a
> consumer's workspace. No tables. There is no runtime: every export is a typed def object, and
> the consumer's `Xano` instance does all encoding at `export()`.

Hosted mode only (the platform is the authorization server; this module is the page it sends users
to). Users sign in with email and password against the consumer's own auth table. For tokens from
an external identity provider, use `mcpServer({ oauth: { mode: "external", ... } })` instead - no
module needed.

## Install

```bash
npm install @xano-sdk/mcp-oauth @xano/sdk
```

`@xano/sdk` is a **peer dependency**, range `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0` - one shared copy only. Tested
against **1.0.0** exactly: the version its golden bundle fixture was generated against. The golden
fixture freezes the bytes this module encodes to (endpoints, headers, the rendered page). It does
not cover what the platform does with them - that is covered by the live runs recorded in
`AGENTS.md`.

`xanosdk init --marketplace @xano-sdk/auth,@xano-sdk/mcp-oauth` writes the `registerMcpOauth`
call with `@xano-sdk/auth`'s `userTable`. It cannot write the `mcpServer({ oauth })` line - add it.

## Quickstart

```ts
// xano/index.ts
import { workspace, workspaceConfig, table, f, tool, mcpServer, s, auth, ref } from "@xano/sdk";
import { registerMcpOauth } from "@xano-sdk/mcp-oauth";

const users = table({
  name: "user",
  auth: true,
  schema: { email: f.email({ required: true }), password: f.password() },
  index: [{ type: "unique", fields: [{ name: "email" }] }],
});

const app = workspace("notes").registerWorkspace(
  workspaceConfig({ name: "notes", env: { MCP_OAUTH_LOGIN_URL: "" } }),
);
app.registerTables([users]);

export const mcpOauth = registerMcpOauth(app, { authTable: users });

const whoami = tool({
  name: "whoami",
  description: "The signed-in user's email.",
  stack: [s.db.get({ table: users, fieldValue: auth("id"), output: ["email"], as: "me" })],
  response: { email: ref("me.email") },
});

const notes = mcpServer({
  name: "notes",
  tools: [{ tool: whoami, auth: users }],
  oauth: mcpOauth.oauth,
});

app.registerTools([whoami]).registerMcpServers([notes]);
export default app;
```

Then, once per environment:

1. `npx xanosdk deploy ./xano/index.ts --allow-empty-env=MCP_OAUTH_LOGIN_URL` - the first deploy,
   before the URL exists.
2. The login URL is the backend URL the deploy prints (it includes `/tenant/<name>` on a tenant or
   ephemeral) plus `mcpOauth.loginQuery.getPath()`, i.e. `/api:mcp-oauth-notes/mcp_oauth/login`.
3. Put `MCP_OAUTH_LOGIN_URL=<that URL>` in `xano/.env` (so later deploys keep it), and set it live:
   `printf '%s' '<that URL>' | npx xanosdk env set MCP_OAUTH_LOGIN_URL`.
4. Connect an MCP client to the server's URL. Redo 2-3 when an ephemeral is re-created.

## Exports

- `registerMcpOauth(app, options): McpOauthDefs` - builds, registers, returns the defs. Once per app.
- `createMcpOauth(options, workspaceName?)` - builds without registering. Pass `canonical`.
- `exportLoginPage({ apiBaseUrl, brandName?, brandColor?, brandLogoUrl?, sharedDomainNotice? }): { html, headers }`
  - the same page, for your own domain.
- `McpOauthDefs`: `{ group, loginQuery, requestQuery, signInQuery, completeQuery, oauth }`.
  `oauth` is `{ mode: "hosted", authTable, loginUrl }` (the SDK's `McpOauthHosted`).
- Constants: `DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT` (`{ max: 5, ttl: 600 }`), `DEFAULT_LOGIN_URL_ENV`
  (`"MCP_OAUTH_LOGIN_URL"`), `SIGN_IN_TOKEN_SECONDS` (`600`), `CONTRACT`.
- Types (erase at compile time): `McpOauthOptions`, `RateLimitOptions`, `BrandingOptions`,
  `ExportLoginPageOptions`, `RenderedPage`, `McpOauthRequestParams`, `McpOauthRequestResponse`,
  `McpOauthSignInBody`, `McpOauthSignInResponse`, `McpOauthCompleteBody`, `McpOauthCompleteResponse`.

## Endpoints

| Route | Auth | Input | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET mcp_oauth/login` | none | `mcp_request?` | the HTML page |
| `GET mcp_oauth/request` | none | `mcp_request` | `{ server_name, client_name, client_logo, callback_host, client_verified, contract }` |
| `POST mcp_oauth/sign_in` | none, rate limited | `{ email, password }` | `{ token }` (600 s session) |
| `POST mcp_oauth/complete` | the auth table | `{ mcp_request, decision: "approve" \| "deny" }` | `{ continue_url }` |

`client_logo` is `""` unless the client is verified. Every `sign_in` refusal is
`403 "Invalid email or password."`.

## Options

- `authTable` (required) - your `table({ auth: true })` handle. Must be the MCP server's auth table;
  the returned `oauth` already is.
- `emailColumn` (`"email"`), `passwordColumn` (`"password"`, must be `f.password()`).
- `activeColumn` - a boolean column that must be true to sign in. Unset: any row with a password.
- `loginUrl` (`env("MCP_OAUTH_LOGIN_URL")`) - an `https:` string or `env("NAME")`.
- `canonical` (`mcp-oauth-<workspace name>`) - pinned so the login URL is stable. Unique per
  INSTANCE across all workspaces; on a deploy conflict, pass another and rebuild the URL.
- `brandName`, `brandColor` (`"#2563eb"`, hex), `brandLogoUrl` (https).
- `sharedDomainNotice` (`true`) - a developer notice on `*.xano.io` hosts.
- `rateLimit` (`{ max: 5, ttl: 600 }` per IP and per email, or `false`) - on by default: `sign_in`
  is a public password check. The window stays inside the 10-minute sign-in.
- `history` (`false`) - request bodies carry a password and a bearer token.

## Calling the endpoints from a typed client

The page does this already; you only need it for a custom page. Types come from the defs:
`McpOauthSignInBody`, `McpOauthSignInResponse`, and so on. Paths come from the defs too -
`mcpOauth.signInQuery.getPath()` - and resolve without a lock because the group's canonical is
pinned.

## Behaviour verified against a live instance

- The page is served as raw HTML by an endpoint, with its CSP and headers intact.
- Browsers hash inline script and style after turning CRLF into LF; the page is LF-only.
- The full hosted flow passed on an ephemeral (a tenant) in both modes, scripted and in Chrome.
- An expired session gets `401` from the endpoint's auth block before `complete` runs.
- The group's default CORS allows the exported page's cross-origin calls, `Authorization` included
  (Chrome).

## Constraints for agents (read before using)

- Pass `mcpOauth.oauth` to `mcpServer({ oauth })` verbatim. Never hand-build the hosted block: the
  platform refuses a sign-in whose session is on any other auth table.
- Call `registerMcpOauth` ONCE per app. One instance serves every MCP server on that auth table.
- Declare `MCP_OAUTH_LOGIN_URL` in `workspaceConfig({ env })`, and use
  `--allow-empty-env=MCP_OAUTH_LOGIN_URL` only for the first deploy. An unset login URL makes every
  sign-in fail with a 503 from the platform.
- Build the login URL from the deployed backend URL plus `loginQuery.getPath()`. On a tenant or
  ephemeral, the backend URL includes `/tenant/<name>`.
- Never use `s.mcp.oauth.complete`'s `unsafe_user_id` in endpoints you add. It skips the platform's
  table and session checks.
- Do not turn `history` on or `rateLimit` off "to debug" in production.
- The sign-in token is a full session on the auth table for 600 s, valid on every endpoint whose
  `auth` is that table. Rules your own login applies (email verification, MFA) are NOT applied;
  only `activeColumn` is.
- For production, host the page on your own domain with `exportLoginPage` and point
  `MCP_OAUTH_LOGIN_URL` at it. Serve it with the returned headers, keep the query string, and do not
  minify or inject into the HTML (the CSP hashes the inline script and style).
- Re-export the page after changing host, canonical, tenant or branding, and after any release whose
  notes say "re-export required".
